# Log

## 2026-06-28 — Initial build from the glioblastoma / neuro-oncology corpus

Built the knowledge base from **72 full-text papers** (PubMed-sourced `.txt`, named by PMID) in
`benchmark_corpus/01_glioblastoma_neuro_oncology/papers/`.

**Result:** 974 typed concept nodes, 2,776 substantive relationship edges (4,547 total including
`reported_in` back-links). `bokf verify` = **ok** (0 errors, 0 warnings; 240 info-level
`edge.missing_direction` hints remain, which are acceptable).

**Node counts by type:** Gene 386, Molecule 112, CellType 91, BiologicalPathway 76,
MethodOrProcedure 76, Phenotype 34, BiomedicalMeasure 20, MolecularClass 19, Anatomy 16, Variant 15,
Disease 12, Dataset 8, MaterialSample 6, Concept 6, SequenceFeature 4, Structure 4, Organism 3,
Device 2, Exposure 2, plus **72 Publication** source nodes (one per ingested paper, each anchored to
its `raw/<id>` source).

**Pipeline (map/reduce):**
1. `bokf convert` of the `papers/` folder → 72 immutable sources under `raw/`.
2. MAP: 37 batches (≤3 papers each, size-bounded), one parallel extraction agent per batch over 5
   waves, each reading a shared extraction prompt + a 123-entry glioblastoma canonical-entity
   dictionary, emitting one typed nodes/edges JSON per paper.
3. REDUCE: deterministic canonicalization (dictionary + formatting-variant merge) → group edges by
   subject → drop invalid-predicate / range-violating / dangling edges → resolve polarity
   contradictions (17 resolved) → cap corroborating sources per triple at 6 (69 capped) →
   `reported_in` back-links → one validated concept page per node. Then `bokf index` / `bokf verify`.

Coverage themes: the glioblastoma tumor microenvironment, tumor-associated macrophages / microglia
(GAMs), M1/M2 polarization, MDSCs and T-cell suppression, proneural→mesenchymal transition, hypoxia,
chemokine axes (CCL2/CCR2, CSF1/CSF1R, CXCL/CXCR), glioma stem cells, and immunotherapy.

Adapt to Persist: Glioblastoma Microenvi.body: This review describes how glioblastoma stem-like cell (GSC) plasticity, driven by hypoxic, invasive and perivascular niches and by dynamic epigenetic modifications, enables adaptation, proneural-to-mesenchymal transition and therapeutic resistance in glioblastoma.
Adapt to Persist: Glioblastoma Microenvi.identifier: Adapt to Persist: Glioblastoma Microenvironment and Epigenetic Regulation on Cell Plasticity

Advancing precision medicine in gliomas.body: Review using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to dissect the glioblastoma tumor microenvironment, detailing how microglia, macrophages, endothelial cells, and T cells interact with tumor cells to drive immunosuppression, growth, and therapy resistance, and how targeting these interactions offers new immunotherapeutic avenues.
Advancing precision medicine in gliomas.identifier: Advancing precision medicine in gliomas through single-cell sequencing: unveiling the complex tumor microenvironment

Allomelanin-based biomimetic nanotherape.body: A biomimetic nanoplatform (AMNP@CLP@CCM) loading the anti-PD-L1 peptide CLP002 into allomelanin nanoparticles and coated with GL261 cancer-cell membrane crosses the blood-brain barrier and homes to orthotopic GBM, where photothermal therapy induces immunogenic cell death and upregulates PD-L1 while CLP002 blocks the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, together boosting T-cell infiltration and significantly inhibiting tumor growth and prolonging survival.
Allomelanin-based biomimetic nanotherape.identifier: Allomelanin-based biomimetic nanotherapeutics for orthotopic glioblastoma targeted photothermal immunotherapy

Cell-lineage controlled epigenetic regul.body: A cross-species ATAC-seq analysis of mouse and patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells shows that chromatin accessibility, driven mainly by distal regulatory elements, separates GSCs into three developmental-origin-determined clusters along a proneural-to-mesenchymal axis with distinct functional properties that predict patient survival.
Cell-lineage controlled epigenetic regul.identifier: Cell-lineage controlled epigenetic regulation in glioblastoma stem cells determines functionally distinct subgroups and predicts patient survival

Cellular and molecular identity of tumor.body: Using Cx3cr1/Ccr2 dual-reporter mice, ~85% of glioblastoma tumor-associated macrophages were shown to be bone marrow-derived monocytes/macrophages (perivascular) recruited early via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, with ~15% resident microglia (peritumoral); heterozygous Ccl2 loss and low tumoral CCL2 prolonged survival.
Cellular and molecular identity of tumor.identifier: Cellular and molecular identity of tumor-associated macrophages in glioblastoma

Chi3l1 Is a Modulator of Glioma Stem Cel.body: CHI3L1 acts as a paracrine microenvironmental factor that binds CD44 on glioma stem cells, activates Akt/beta-catenin/STAT3 signaling and a MAZ-regulated transcriptional network, driving GSCs toward poised mesenchymal states; a blocking anti-CHI3L1 antibody reduces glioblastoma xenograft growth by more than 60% and prolongs survival.
Chi3l1 Is a Modulator of Glioma Stem Cel.identifier: Chi3l1 Is a Modulator of Glioma Stem Cell States and a Therapeutic Target in Glioblastoma

Context-Dependent Glioblastoma-Macrophag.body: This opinion article reviews how specific tumor-suppressor (PTEN, NF1, TP53) and oncogene (EGFR, CLOCK) alterations in glioblastoma cells recruit and polarize glioblastoma-associated macrophages/microglia (GAMs), and reciprocally how GAMs sustain glioma stem cell stemness and promote GBM progression, framing this context-dependent symbiosis as a therapeutic target.
Context-Dependent Glioblastoma-Macrophag.identifier: Context-Dependent Glioblastoma-Macrophage/microglia Symbiosis and Associated Mechanisms

Cross-talk between disulfidptosis and im.body: Using TCGA and CGGA data, the authors built a six-gene (CD276, TNFRSF14, TNFSF14, TNFSF4, CD40, TNFRSF18) disulfidptosis-related immune checkpoint risk signature that predicts overall survival and immunotherapy sensitivity in glioblastoma; the high-risk group shows an immunosuppressive TME with TAMs, neutrophils, exhausted CD8+ T cells, angiogenesis, ECM remodeling and EMT, and CD276 was validated by IHC as negatively correlated with survival.
Cross-talk between disulfidptosis and im.identifier: Cross-talk between disulfidptosis and immune check point genes defines the tumor microenvironment for the prediction of prognosis and immunotherapies in glioblastoma

Crosstalk between glioblastoma and tumor.body: This review summarizes autocrine and paracrine ligand-receptor pathways in the glioblastoma microenvironment that drive proneural-mesenchymal transition (PMT), and discusses therapies targeting these pathways and why GBM-targeted therapy fails.
Crosstalk between glioblastoma and tumor.identifier: Crosstalk between glioblastoma and tumor microenvironment drives proneural-mesenchymal transition through ligand-receptor interactions

Dissecting the immunosuppressive tumor m.body: A patient-specific microfluidic GBM-on-a-Chip system shows that mesenchymal GBM has a more immunosuppressive niche (abundant CD163+ M2-TAMs, high PD-1/PD-L1, TGF-β1, IL-10, CSF-1) than proneural GBM, and that combining the CSF-1R inhibitor BLZ945 with the anti-PD-1 antibody nivolumab reverses immunosuppression and increases GBM apoptosis.
Dissecting the immunosuppressive tumor m.identifier: Dissecting the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments in Glioblastoma-on-a-Chip for optimized PD-1 immunotherapy

Dual role of ARPC1B in regulating the ne.body: ARPC1B is identified as a key macrophage-associated prognostic gene in glioblastoma whose high expression correlates with malignancy, TAM infiltration and poor survival; macrophage-expressed and glioma-intrinsic ARPC1B reciprocally promote glioma migration, invasion and EMT and macrophage recruitment via an IFNγ-IRF2-ARPC1B positive-feedback axis.

Gene regulatory network topology governs.body: Single-cell inference of transcription-factor regulatory network topology in patient-derived glioma stem-like cells shows that the architecture of the core TF-TF network, not the initial cell-state composition, governs proneural-to-mesenchymal transition and pitavastatin resistance; this topology can be exploited to rationally design sequential combinatorial treatments (siRNA TF knockdown or vinflunine) that disrupt acquired resistance.
Gene regulatory network topology governs.identifier: Gene regulatory network topology governs resistance and treatment escape in glioma stem-like cells

Glioblastoma microenvironment—from biolo.body: A review describing the molecular and cellular heterogeneity of the glioblastoma tumor microenvironment across spatial niches (perivascular, hypoxic, and invasive edge) and surveying TME-targeting therapeutic strategies in gliomas.

Glioblastomas acquire myeloid-affiliated.body: Serial transplantation of engineered mouse glioma stem cells through immunocompetent hosts shows that immune attack drives stable, epigenetically-fixed transcriptional changes (epigenetic immunoediting) that hijack the myeloid transcription factor IRF8 and chemokine secretion, remodeling the tumor microenvironment toward a macrophage-rich, immunosuppressive mesenchymal state; the same IFN-driven, hypomethylated signature marks human mesenchymal GBM.
Glioblastomas acquire myeloid-affiliated.identifier: Glioblastomas acquire myeloid-affiliated transcriptional programs via epigenetic immunoediting to elicit immune evasion

Glioma-associated microglia/macrophages.body: A review of how glioma-associated microglia/macrophages (GAMs) are recruited by glioma cells, polarize to a tumor-promoting M2 state, and drive invasion, angiogenesis, immunosuppression and GSC support, plus immunotherapies targeting GAMs (CSF1R, STAT3, SDF-1 inhibitors).
Glioma-associated microglia/macrophages.identifier: Glioma-associated microglia/macrophages (GAMs) in glioblastoma: Immune function in the tumor microenvironment and implications for immunotherapy

Glioma-derived CCL2 and CCL7 mediate mig.body: Glioma-produced chemokines CCL2 and CCL7 redundantly drive CCR2-dependent migration of bone marrow-derived CCR2+/CX3CR1+ M-MDSCs into the glioblastoma microenvironment, where these cells suppress CD4+ and CD8+ T cells; combined CCL2/CCL7 targeting reduces their infiltration and high CCL2/CCL7 expression predicts poor survival.
Glioma-derived CCL2 and CCL7 mediate mig.identifier: Glioma-derived CCL2 and CCL7 mediate migration of immune suppressive CCR2+/CX3CR1+ M-MDSCs into the tumor microenvironment in a redundant manner

Glioma-derived M-CSF and IL-34 license M.body: Glioma-secreted CSF1R ligands M-CSF (CSF1) and IL-34 drive differentiation of CCR2+/CX3CR1+ monocytic MDSCs from bone marrow, and these M-MDSCs suppress CD8+ T cell proliferation in an iNOS/NOS-dependent manner, with adenosine (CD39/CD73) pathways adding spatially heterogeneous suppression in the glioblastoma microenvironment.
Glioma-derived M-CSF and IL-34 license M.identifier: Glioma-derived M-CSF and IL-34 license M-MDSCs to suppress CD8+ T cells in a NOS-dependent manner

Human Mesenchymal glioblastomas are char.body: Using TCGA gene expression and IHC of 56 human GBM samples, the Mesenchymal subtype showed the highest infiltration of TAM (IBA1+), CD8+, CD3+ and FOXP3+ T cells; high AIF1/IBA1 expression conferred worse prognosis in Proneural but a survival benefit in Mesenchymal GBM.
Human Mesenchymal glioblastomas are char.identifier: Human Mesenchymal glioblastomas are characterized by an increased immune cell presence compared to Proneural and Classical tumors

Hypoxia Contributes to Poor Prognosis in.body: Single-cell and bulk RNA-seq analysis of primary IDH-wildtype glioblastoma shows hypoxia is an independent poor-prognostic factor that drives tumor cells toward a MES-like state and suppresses immune cell activity, notably by polarizing tumor-associated macrophages from M1 toward M2 and strengthening inhibitory tumor-immune interactions.
Hypoxia Contributes to Poor Prognosis in.identifier: Hypoxia Contributes to Poor Prognosis in Primary IDH-wt GBM by Inducing Tumor Cells MES-Like Transformation Trend and Inhibiting Immune Cells Activity

Hypoxia drives shared and distinct trans.body: RNA-seq of two hypoxia-responsive patient-derived GBM stem cell lines reveals shared hypoxia genes (glycolysis, angiogenesis, autophagy) plus patient-specific migration/immunosuppression programs; applying the shared signature to scRNA-seq shows hypoxia shifts IDH-wildtype glioma cells to a mesenchymal state and IDH-mutant cells to an astrocyte-like state.
Hypoxia drives shared and distinct trans.identifier: Hypoxia drives shared and distinct transcriptomic changes in two invasive glioma stem cell lines

Hypoxia enhances migration and invasion.body: In GBM cell lines, hypoxia induces a mesenchymal shift and enhanced invasion through a HIF1α-ZEB1 signaling axis; digoxin or knockdown of HIF1α or ZEB1 prevents this transition.
Hypoxia enhances migration and invasion.identifier: Hypoxia enhances migration and invasion in glioblastoma by promoting a mesenchymal shift mediated by the HIF1α-ZEB1 axis

Hypoxia-driven M2-polarized macrophages.body: Hypoxia drives HIF1A-dependent M2 polarization of TAMs, which transfer circ_0003137-enriched extracellular vesicles to glioblastoma cells; circ_0003137 binds PTBP1 to stabilize PLOD3 and promote EMT, migration, and invasion, and an sh-circ_0003137 nanoplatform inhibits tumor progression.

Immunogenetics of glioblastoma: the futu.body: A review describing how molecular profiling and immunophenotyping of glioblastoma (IDH status, subtype-specific immune-evasion mechanisms, immunosuppressive TME) may guide personalized therapies, including emerging targets such as STAT3, IDO, TGF-beta and checkpoint inhibitors.
Immunogenetics of glioblastoma: the futu.identifier: Immunogenetics of glioblastoma: the future of personalized patient management

Immunotherapy drives mesenchymal tumor c.body: Paired single-cell RNA-seq of glioblastoma patients treated with the PD-1 inhibitor nivolumab reveals an immunotherapy-induced shift to mesenchymal-like tumor cells with increased TAMs and proliferative/exhausted T cells; a derived latent-immune signature (~18% of GBMs) predicts shorter overall survival after checkpoint therapy.
Immunotherapy drives mesenchymal tumor c.identifier: Immunotherapy drives mesenchymal tumor cell state shift and TME immune response in glioblastoma patients

Inflammation and lymphocyte infiltration.body: RNA-seq and flow cytometry of high-grade glioma biopsies and PBMCs show that increased inflammation and immune infiltration—especially tumor lymphocyte infiltration—are associated with shorter overall survival; the lymphocyte component is an independent prognostic predictor.
Inflammation and lymphocyte infiltration.identifier: Inflammation and lymphocyte infiltration are associated with shorter survival in patients with high-grade glioma

Integrated single-cell transcriptomic an.body: Integrative scRNA-seq analysis and ex vivo validation show that GPNMB-high macrophages, derived from monocytes, drive a proneural-to-mesenchymal cell-state transition in glioblastoma tumor cells and ineffectively retain T cells, impeding their activation by dendritic cells.
Integrated single-cell transcriptomic an.identifier: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analyses reveal that GPNMB-high macrophages promote PN-MES transition and impede T cell activation in GBM

Integrative spatial analysis reveals a m.body: Combining spatial transcriptomics (Visium) and spatial proteomics (CODEX), the authors define glioma cellular states and show they are spatially organized into local state-enriched environments, recurrent pairwise state associations, and a global five-layered architecture driven by hypoxia as a long-range tissue organizer; tumors lacking hypoxia (e.g., IDH-mutant glioma) are less organized.
Integrative spatial analysis reveals a m.identifier: Integrative spatial analysis reveals a multi-layered organization of glioblastoma

Interactions between cancer cells and im.body: Macrophage-derived Oncostatin M (OSM) signaling through OSMR or LIFR in complex with GP130 activates STAT3 to drive glioblastoma cells into a mesenchymal-like (MES-like) state; these MES-like states are reciprocally linked to a mesenchymal macrophage program and to increased MHC expression and cytotoxic T-cell activity.
Interactions between cancer cells and im.identifier: Interactions between cancer cells and immune cells drive transitions to mesenchymal-like states in glioblastoma

Macrophage-tumor cell intertwine drives.body: This Cancer Cell preview highlights work showing that macrophages induce glioblastoma cells to transition into a mesenchymal-like state via macrophage-derived Oncostatin M signaling through OSMR/LIFR-GP130 and STAT3 activation, forming a reciprocal loop that also drives mesenchymal programs in macrophages and increased cytotoxic T-cell presence.
Macrophage-tumor cell intertwine drives.identifier: Macrophage-tumor cell intertwine drives the transition into a mesenchymal-like cellular state of glioblastoma

Macrophages and microglia: the cerberus.body: A review of the origin, heterogeneity, and pro-tumorigenic roles of glioblastoma tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) — comprising brain-resident microglia and bone marrow-derived macrophages — which support tumor proliferation, drive immunosuppression, and promote vasogenic cerebral edema, and the prospects for therapeutically targeting them.
Macrophages and microglia: the cerberus.identifier: Macrophages and microglia: the cerberus of glioblastoma

Macrophages in Glioblastoma Development.body: Review of glioblastoma-associated macrophages (GAMs) — comprising resident microglia and bone marrow-derived macrophages — detailing their M1/M2 polarization, protumorigenic crosstalk with GBM cells in malignancy, angiogenesis and drug resistance, and emerging GAM-targeted therapies (phagocytosis checkpoints, CSF-1R depletion, reprogramming, CAR-M).
Macrophages in Glioblastoma Development.identifier: Macrophages in Glioblastoma Development and Therapy: A Double-Edged Sword

Macrophages in Recurrent Glioblastoma as.body: This review summarizes how glioma-associated macrophages, especially M2-polarized subtypes, promote tumor progression, therapy resistance and immunosuppression in recurrent GBM, with high macrophage infiltration correlating with worse overall survival and offering targets for therapy.
Macrophages in Recurrent Glioblastoma as.identifier: Macrophages in Recurrent Glioblastoma as a Prognostic Factor in the Synergistic System of the Tumor Microenvironment

Magnesium-Phenolic Nanoeditor Refining G.body: A BBB-penetrating Mg2+@MK-8931@MPP nanoeditor repolarizes M2-like glioblastoma-associated macrophages (via the BACE1 inhibitor MK-8931) to recruit CTLs, while Mg2+ enhances CTL cytotoxicity through TCR/FAK/ERK1/2 signaling and anti-NK1.1 antibody sustains CTL killing, jointly improving glioblastoma control and survival in mouse models.
Magnesium-Phenolic Nanoeditor Refining G.identifier: Magnesium-Phenolic Nanoeditor Refining Gliomatous T Cells for Metalloimmunotherapy

Mechanosensitive expression of the mesen.body: In primary patient-derived glioblastoma cell lines, expression of the mesenchymal marker CTGF is induced by increasing substrate stiffness (peaking at 8 kPa) via YAP/TAZ nuclear accumulation, and this mechanosensitive CTGF induction occurs prior to cell spreading and independently of actin filament polymerization.
Mechanosensitive expression of the mesen.identifier: Mechanosensitive expression of the mesenchymal subtype marker connective tissue growth factor in glioblastoma

Metabolic/Proteomic Signature Defines Tw.body: Gene expression, NMR metabolomic and reverse-phase protein array profiling of patient-derived glioblastoma stem-like cells defines proneural-like (GSf) and mesenchymal-like (GSr) subtypes; in TCGA, SRC/HER3 activation marks a better-prognosis subgroup whereas RPS6 (mTOR effector) activation marks a worse-prognosis subgroup.
Metabolic/Proteomic Signature Defines Tw.identifier: Metabolic/Proteomic Signature Defines Two Glioblastoma Subtypes With Different Clinical Outcome

Nanoparticle-mediated blockade of CXCL12.body: An iRGD-modified polymeric nanoparticle co-delivering the CXCR4 antagonist AMD3100 and the small-molecule PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor BMS-1 crossed the blood-brain barrier and reprogrammed the immunosuppressive glioblastoma microenvironment (reduced TAMs, MDSCs and Tregs, increased M1/M2 ratio and CD8+ T cells), suppressing tumor growth and extending survival in orthotopic GL261 GBM mice, with MRI radiomic texture features detecting early immune microenvironment changes.
Nanoparticle-mediated blockade of CXCL12.identifier: Nanoparticle-mediated blockade of CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling enhances glioblastoma immunotherapy: Monitoring early responses with MRI radiomics

Network Analyses of Brain Tumor Patients.body: Using snRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq and phosphoproteomics from 92 GBM patients, the authors construct cell-state protein-protein interaction networks and a Boolean model; in silico knockouts plus machine learning identify TP53/PTEN loss, STAT3, and TFAP2A silencing as drivers of NPC-to-MES cell-state transitions, nominating targets for cell-state-directed therapy.
Network Analyses of Brain Tumor Patients.identifier: Network Analyses of Brain Tumor Patients' Multiomic Data Reveals Pharmacological Opportunities to Alter Cell State Transitions

Network Analyses of Brain Tumor Patients.body: Integrating snRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq and phosphoproteomics from GBM patients, the authors built cell-state-specific protein-protein interaction networks and a Boolean model whose in silico knockouts and machine-learning predictions nominate drivers (TP53/PTEN loss, STAT3, TFAP2A) of NPC-to-MES cell-state transitions as targets for cell-state-directed therapy.

Phagocytosis of Glioma Cells Enhances th.body: Using single-cell RNA-seq, WES, CyTOF and in vitro coculture, the study shows that bone marrow-derived macrophages phagocytose glioma cells to form double-positive TAMs that adopt an M2-like, immunosuppressive phenotype upregulating PD-L1, PD-L2 and CD276 and suppressing T-cell proliferation.
Phagocytosis of Glioma Cells Enhances th.identifier: Phagocytosis of Glioma Cells Enhances the Immunosuppressive Phenotype of Bone Marrow-Derived Macrophages

Phenotype switching in glioblastoma prom.body: This Cancer Discovery Research Watch summary of Wang, Jung, Babikir et al. reports a single-cell multiomic atlas of matched primary-recurrent glioblastoma showing that recurrence is characterized by a shift to a mesenchymal cell state driven by AP1, that ionizing radiation induces AP1 and MES hallmark genes as a therapy-escape mechanism, and that T-cell abundance at recurrence correlates with improved survival and hypermutation.
Phenotype switching in glioblastoma prom.identifier: Phenotype switching in glioblastoma promotes therapy escape

Proneural-Mesenchymal Transition: Phenot.body: Review describing how proneural-to-mesenchymal transition (PMT) in glioblastoma, driven by master regulators (STAT3, C/EBPβ, TAZ) and the TNF-α/NF-κB axis under treatment pressure, confers an aggressive mesenchymal phenotype and multitherapy resistance.
Proneural-Mesenchymal Transition: Phenot.identifier: Proneural-Mesenchymal Transition: Phenotypic Plasticity to Acquire Multitherapy Resistance in Glioblastoma

Protein Analysis of Glioblastoma Primary.body: In paired initial and posttreatment glioblastoma, a subset of recurrent tumors acquired increased mesenchymal protein markers (CD44, pSTAT3, YKL-40), which was associated with shorter progression-free survival after recurrence, while high Ki-67 and EGFR in initial tumors predicted worse survival.
Protein Analysis of Glioblastoma Primary.identifier: Protein Analysis of Glioblastoma Primary and Posttreatment Pairs Suggests a Mesenchymal Shift at Recurrence

Q-Cell Glioblastoma Resource: Proteomics.body: Mass-spectrometry proteomic profiling of 13 primary IDH-wildtype Q-Cell glioblastoma models in 3D culture quantified 6167 proteins and confirmed that the four GBM cellular states (MES-like, NPC-like, OPC-like, AC-like) are represented and maintained, with a paired primary/recurrent model showing a shift toward a more mesenchymal state at recurrence.
Q-Cell Glioblastoma Resource: Proteomics.identifier: Q-Cell Glioblastoma Resource: Proteomics Analysis Reveals Unique Cell-States Are Maintained in 3D Culture

Regulation of tumor immune suppression a.body: CXCL1 and CXCL2 are overexpressed in high-grade and recurrent GBM, recruiting MDSCs and M2 TAMs via CXCR2 to suppress CD8+ T cells and driving S100A9-mediated prosurvival signaling; antibody blockade of CXCL1/2 restores antitumor immunity, sensitizes to temozolomide, and prolongs survival in mouse models.
Regulation of tumor immune suppression a.identifier: Regulation of tumor immune suppression and cancer cell survival by CXCL1/2 elevation in glioblastoma multiforme

Resident stroma-secreted chemokine CCL2.body: Using a patient-derived stroma xenograft model of oral cancer, resident stroma-secreted CCL2 recruits CCR2+ myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) into the tumor microenvironment via the CCL2/CCR2 axis, which is blocked by CCL2 synthesis inhibition or CCR2 antagonism.
Resident stroma-secreted chemokine CCL2.identifier: Resident stroma-secreted chemokine CCL2 governs myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the tumor microenvironment

Revealing and Harnessing Tumour-Associat.body: This review describes the transcriptional, ontogenetic and spatial heterogeneity of tumour-associated microglia/macrophages (TAMs) in glioblastoma and argues that this diversity, beyond the simple M1/M2 dichotomy, must be harnessed for effective TAM-targeted immunotherapies.
Revealing and Harnessing Tumour-Associat.identifier: Revealing and Harnessing Tumour-Associated Microglia/Macrophage Heterogeneity in Glioblastoma

Role of myeloid cells in the immunosuppr.body: Review describing how glioma-associated macrophages/microglia (GAMs) and other myeloid cells are recruited to and polarized within the glioblastoma tumor microenvironment to drive immunosuppression, angiogenesis, invasion and therapy resistance, and surveying myeloid-targeted immunotherapeutic strategies.

Signal Pathways Involved in the Interact.body: A review of the bidirectional signaling between glioblastoma cells and tumor-associated macrophages/microglia, covering chemokine-driven TAM recruitment, polarization toward an immunosuppressive M2-like pro-tumor phenotype, TAM-promoted glioma proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis, and TAM-targeted therapeutic strategies.
Signal Pathways Involved in the Interact.identifier: Signal Pathways Involved in the Interaction Between Tumor-Associated Macrophages/TAMs and Glioblastoma Cells

Single-Cell Transcriptomics Revealed Sub.body: scRNA-seq of 7 IDH-wildtype GBM patients showed NPC2-like cells are the proliferative cells of origin, while hypoxia-response MES1/MES2-like tumor cells and TAM-1 macrophages drive angiogenesis, invasion, M2 polarization and poor prognosis via ligand-receptor signaling.
Single-Cell Transcriptomics Revealed Sub.identifier: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Revealed Subtype-Specific Tumor Immune Microenvironments in Human Glioblastomas

Single-cell chromatin accessibility prof.body: Single-cell and bulk ATAC-seq of primary IDH-wildtype glioblastomas and patient-derived glioma stem cells define three chromatin-driven GSC states (Reactive, Constructive, Invasive) governed by distinct essential transcription factors; the Invasive state is the most invasive and predicts poorer patient survival.
Single-cell chromatin accessibility prof.identifier: Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling of glioblastoma identifies an invasive cancer stem cell population associated with lower survival

Spatial transcriptomics reveals segregat.body: Paired snRNA-seq and Visium spatial transcriptomics of three GBM patients show that tumor cell states (OPC-like, NPC-like, AC-like, MES-like) segregate into distinct spatial niches, with OPC-like cells enriched perivascularly and macrophage-rich perinecrotic regions being markedly immunosuppressive.
Spatial transcriptomics reveals segregat.identifier: Spatial transcriptomics reveals segregation of tumor cell states in glioblastoma and marked immunosuppression within the perinecrotic niche

Stem cell signature in glioblastoma: the.body: Review describing two mutually exclusive glioma stem cell subtypes (proneural and mesenchymal) with distinct signaling, metabolic, and radioresistance properties, and the plasticity/transdifferentiation between them that drives therapy resistance in high-grade glioma.
Stem cell signature in glioblastoma: the.identifier: Stem cell signature in glioblastoma: therapeutic development for a moving target

The Impact of Hypoxia and Mesenchymal Tr.body: A review describing how hypoxia and HIF signaling drive mesenchymal transformation, cancer stem cell maintenance, angiogenesis, and treatment resistance in glioblastoma, and proposing combined targeting of hypoxia and mesenchymal pathways as a therapeutic strategy.
The Impact of Hypoxia and Mesenchymal Tr.identifier: The Impact of Hypoxia and Mesenchymal Transition on Glioblastoma Pathogenesis and Cancer Stem Cells Regulation

The Importance of M1- and M2-Polarized M.body: This review synthesizes mechanisms by which tumor-associated macrophages polarize toward tumor-suppressive M1 or tumor-supportive M2 states in glioblastoma, covering signaling axes (Galectin/Gal-9/Tim3, chemerin/CMKLR1, MTA/A2B, HMGB1/RAGE, BACE1/IL-6/STAT3, B2M/PI3K, FGF20/beta-catenin, CHI3L1/Gal3, MFG-E8/ITGB3, exosomes), and proposes reprogramming M2 to M1 as a therapeutic strategy.
The Importance of M1- and M2-Polarized M.identifier: The Importance of M1- and M2-Polarized Macrophages in Glioma and as Potential Treatment Targets

The Phenotypes of Proliferating Glioblas.body: Single-cell RNA/ATAC sequencing of 28 gliomas shows IDH-wildtype GBM stem-like cells lie on a single proneural-to-mesenchymal axis, with lineage tracing supporting mesenchymal GSCs as progenitors of proneural GSCs; the mGSC signature correlates with inferior survival and dual targeting of both GSC phenotypes is more effective.
The Phenotypes of Proliferating Glioblas.identifier: The Phenotypes of Proliferating Glioblastoma Cells Reside on a Single Axis of Variation

Tumor-Associated Macrophages as Major Pl.body: This review describes how circulating monocytes are recruited and polarized into M2-like tumor-associated macrophages that promote tumor angiogenesis, invasion, metastasis, immunosuppression, and chemoresistance, and reviews TAM-targeting therapeutic strategies.
Tumor-Associated Macrophages as Major Pl.identifier: Tumor-Associated Macrophages as Major Players in the Tumor Microenvironment

Tumor-associated macrophages induce vasc.body: M2-polarized tumor-associated macrophages promote vasculogenic mimicry in U87 glioblastoma cells by upregulating COX-2 and activating the PGE2/EP1/PKC pathway; COX-2 inhibition or knockdown impairs VM in vitro and in xenografts, and high COX-2 correlates with shorter progression-free survival.
Tumor-associated macrophages induce vasc.identifier: Tumor-associated macrophages induce vasculogenic mimicry of glioblastoma multiforme through cyclooxygenase-2 activation

Tumor-associated microglia and macrophag.body: This review describes the origin, polarization, and pro-tumor functions of tumor-associated microglia and macrophages (TAMs) in glioblastoma and summarizes therapeutic strategies that deplete, repolarize, enhance phagocytosis of, or reduce recruitment of TAMs.
Tumor-associated microglia and macrophag.identifier: Tumor-associated microglia and macrophages in glioblastoma: From basic insights to therapeutic opportunities
